title: Adaptive tail-hedging batcher for interleaved short/long turns
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Mixed workloads with interleaved short user prompts and long model responses cause the continuous batcher to either: (a) wait and increase P95 latency for short-turn requests, or (b) aggressively coalesce resulting in large KV cache pressure and GPU memory fragmentation. Goal: implement an adaptive 'tail-hedging' scheduling mode that hedges on expected long-turn completions while preserving fast-path latency for short-turn prompts and reducing KV cache churn.
acceptance_criteria: P50 latency for <64-token prompts increases by <= 5% relative to current baseline under mixed workload (50% short, 50% long)
P95 latency for <64-token prompts improves by >= 10% vs baseline without tail-hedging under 30-70 short-long ratio
GPU VRAM variance across batch windows reduced by >= 15% (fewer peak spikes) when running representative replay
KV cache eviction rate decreases by >= 20% for long-dialogue customers due to staggered-prefix caching
Strategy validated in canary fleet (10% host pool) with monitoring dashboards and rollback flag
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight per-slot tail-hedge timer: short requests get a short hedging window (2-6 ms) while suspected long-turn continuations are given a longer soft-reservation (20-80 ms) before coalescing
Add 'staggered-prefix caching' where KV reservations for long responses are soft-pinned and only fully materialized when per-slot steady-state is detected
Implement KV shard soft-partitioning: avoid global eviction by giving high-residency shards temporary lease tokens to reduce cross-customer compaction
Introduce a small slot-preemption budget to allow urgent (<64 token) requests to preempt a coalescing slot if latency SLOs risk being breached
Add histogram-based per-route length predictors (lightweight model) to inform hedging windows and cache prefetch decisions
Ensure all new timers and heuristics are feature-flagged and controlled by runtime config for fast rollback
experiments: Microbench: synthetic replay with three traffic mixes (80/20 short-long, 50/50, 20/80) using current production prefixes
Memory stress: run long-dialogue replay (avg 2k tokens) on 8-GPU node families (A100/MI250 equiv) and measure fragmentation via slab-alloc histograms
A/B Canary: 10% cohort on dedicated pool with canary config enabling hedging + soft-partitioning; compare against baseline for 48 hours
Eviction sensitivity: sweep soft-reservation timeouts (20/40/80 ms) and measure KV eviction-per-minute and get per-token cost delta
metrics_targets: Throughput target: <= 5% throughput degradation for mixed traffic vs baseline
Cost target: net token-serving cost change within +/-2% after hedging and reduced eviction
Latency targets: P50 and P95 targets as in acceptance_criteria
KV metrics: eviction-rate, cold-hit-rate, per-shard eviction variance
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive hedging reduces rework for long responses but increases latency for short prompts; we mitigate by dynamic hedging windows and preemption budgets
We deliberately avoid heavyweight ML models; length predictor must be sub-millisecond and have <1KB state per-slot
KV soft-partitioning may increase temporary memory footprint; we will measure cost delta and have a hard cap fallback that reverts to global LRU eviction
This feature intersects with Dedicated pool policy; coordinate config exposure with Dedicated team (privacy of shard leases)
Fallback plan: if memory inflation >10% or P95 for short prompts regresses >15%, toggle off hedging and enable conservative soft-reservation
